channel.title: GLab Articles
channel.description: Guang’s personal profile and public knowledge hub for complete projects with embedded guides, technical articles, research notes and documented experiments across technology, cybersecurity, AI, networking, sustainability and engineering.

item.title: Better light begins by protecting the dark
item.description: How careful placement, shielding, warm colour, dimming, and simple controls can make outdoor lighting more useful to people and less disruptive to wildlife.

item.title: Keep the music, protect the hearing
item.description: Safe-listening tools and habits that preserve the joy and detail of music without treating hearing as an unlimited resource.

item.title: Passkeys move security closer to how people actually live
item.description: A practical guide to phishing-resistant sign-in, safer account recovery, and the human habits that still matter after passwords begin to disappear.

item.title: The greenest upgrade may be the one you do not buy
item.description: A practical path for keeping electronics useful longer, protecting personal data, and sending truly finished devices into responsible reuse or recycling.

item.title: The most responsible AI may be the smallest one that works
item.description: A decision framework for using AI where it creates real value, choosing the lightest capable system, and keeping people accountable for the result.

item.title: A soil sensor is a question, not an answer
item.description: How growers can combine moisture sensors, field observation, weather, and simple records to irrigate with more confidence and less false precision.

item.title: What the soil taught the sensor
item.description: Field notes on calibration, false precision, and why a farmer’s hand can be the best instrument in the loop.

item.title: Responsible AI begins before the model
item.description: A practical framework for deciding whether an AI system should exist, what it should optimize, and who gets to question it.

item.title: In praise of small, understandable tools
item.description: A note about software that can be held in one person’s head—and why constraint can be a form of care.

item.title: Security is a form of care
item.description: Moving beyond fear-driven security toward systems that respect attention, dignity, and ordinary human behavior.
